The committee assigned AID operating and funding responsibility except for covert aspects and selected Defense programs.

approved_claims.article_excerpt: President John F. Kennedy addressed that tension directly in NSAM 132, signed February 19, 1962. His memorandum went to Fowler Hamilton, the administrator of AID. approved_claims.source_excerpt: I recognize that such programs may seem marginal in terms of focusing our energies on those key sectors which will contribute most to sustained economic growth. I went back to the 1962 records behind the early U.S. foreign-police program.

Follow four decisions across 1962, and a police system takes shape in plain sight.

NSAM 132 was dated February 19, 1962.

NSAM 162 was dated June 19, 1962.

The July 20, 1962 committee called police programs a neglected part of countering subversion and insurgency.

The committee assigned AID operating and funding responsibility except for covert aspects and selected Defense programs.

The committee required AID to report implementation progress by December 1, 1962.

My takeaway is narrower than ‘USAID was the CIA.’ The documents show an AID-led overt program inside a wider internal-defense structure, with covert aspects explicitly carved out. I would be interested in primary records that sharpen or challenge that boundary.

Primary records that sharpen or challenge this reading are welcome.
